findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to a datetime, crashing any non-empty page
findings.body: The endpoint sends `order_by="-datetime"` to this paginator, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime` for each AuditLogEntry. `math.floor()`/`math.ceil()` raise TypeError on a datetime. `build_cursor` calls this key function on the results, so with `optimized_pagination=true` every organization that has at least one audit entry gets a 500. Only the empty-result case avoids the call. DateTimePaginator.get_item_key avoids this by converting the datetime to a millisecond epoch value. This class did not copy that logic, so it cannot serve its only use case. Subclassing DateTimePaginator or porting its conversion would fix it.

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which is then bound against a DateTimeField
findings.body: DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor converts the millisecond cursor value back into a timezone-aware datetime. This class returns `cursor.value` unchanged. `build_queryset` then appends that int to the `extra(where=...)` params against `auditlogentry.datetime`, so any request carrying a next/prev cursor either fails at the database (timestamp compared with integer) or fails Django's DateTimeField validation. Pagination past the first page cannot work on this path.

findings.title: Negative cursor offset is passed straight into a queryset slice, which Django rejects
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is the raw negative offset and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is evaluated. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices and raises an error, so the request returns a 500. The branch that is supposed to reach data beyond normal pagination bounds therefore never returns data. A user can reach this with any crafted cursor string whose offset is negative, provided the advanced flag is set.

findings.title: Comments justify exposing data beyond pagination bounds on the claim that queryset-level checks exist, which is false
findings.body: The comments at lines 878-879 say the negative-offset branch 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' and that this 'is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'. The queryset here is only filtered by organization_id (organization_auditlogs.py line 48). The role check that enables the mode is in the endpoint (line 71). Nothing checks permissions at the queryset level. The intent is a privilege-gated path that widens what an admin can reach, and its safety argument is wrong and unreviewed. The branch should be removed or its authorization model explicitly designed and documented.

findings.title: Negative offsets are silently clamped to 0 in BasePaginator for every paginator, not only the new one
findings.body: The change to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` affects BasePaginator.get_result, which DateTimePaginator, Paginator and every other cursor paginator inherit. It is not gated by the new query parameter. Before this change, a non-prev cursor with a negative offset (reachable through Cursor.from_string) raised a slicing error. Now it silently returns the first page with a cursor built from the original negative offset. The comment at lines 179-181 says negative offsets are being allowed, but the code does the opposite, clamping them. The comment and the global behavior change both need to be reconsidered, and the change should be separated from this feature.

findings.title: organization_context.member is dereferenced without a None check
findings.body: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional, since a requester may not be a member of the organization. The expression `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` only avoids the dereference when the user is a superuser. For any other requester with no membership record, this raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Whether OrganizationAuditPermission guarantees membership for non-superusers is not visible in this diff, so this needs a None guard or a confirmed invariant.

findings.title: Privileged mode is gated on the raw is_superuser flag rather than an active superuser session
findings.body: The gate uses `request.user.is_superuser` directly. Sentry's superuser pattern normally checks an elevated, session-scoped superuser state (for example via is_active_superuser(request)). Using the raw user flag can grant the advanced mode to a superuser who has not elevated in this session. The impact is limited while the advanced path is broken, but the gate should follow the codebase's superuser convention.

findings.title: Comment claims a Cursor behavior change that the diff does not make
findings.body: The added comment says the Cursor now 'allows negative offsets ... enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets'. The code line below it, `self.offset = int(offset)`, is unchanged. The class already accepted negative offsets, and nothing in the change makes pagination more efficient. The comment documents a nonexistent optimization and should be removed.

findings.title: New paginator, query-parameter path and negative-offset behavior change have no tests
findings.body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, a new `optimized_pagination` branch in the endpoint, an advanced-features gate, and a global change to BasePaginator offset handling, but adds no tests. The first basic use (one page of audit entries with the param set) crashes, as described in the get_item_key and value_from_cursor findings. A simple endpoint test would have caught it. Tests are also needed for the default DateTimePaginator path, which the BasePaginator change now affects.

findings.title: PR description is a placeholder and the 'performance' framing is unsupported
findings.body: The description is only 'Test 1', so nothing explains why the endpoint gets an undocumented `optimized_pagination` query parameter or who it is for. The code comments at lines 68-75 call this a performance optimization, but the optimized branch issues the same ORM queries as DateTimePaginator (its only real difference is the broken negative-offset branch), and no measurements are included. The title and comments overstate what the change does.
